articles.title: Xi, Putin, and Trump meeting concludes with vague commitments, but strong symbolism
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Chinese President Xi Jinping held the first ever trilateral summit of Russia, China, and the US on the sidelines of the ongoing Asia-Pacific Economic Council (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19. The meeting, attended by Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump, ended with a joint Declaration towards Peace with all three countries agreeing to find ways to work together on common issues including the need for reforms in the UN, global energy security, and rising nuclear risk. The declaration also talked about the principles of the operation of the International Criminal Court (ICC) and underlined the immunity for top state officials. articles.title: The daily reality of Israel’s mass extermination of life in Gaza
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: As Israel’s military aggression on the Gaza Strip enters its fourth year, devastating details continue to emerge regarding how every facet of daily life in Gaza has been engineered to maximize Palestinian casualties. In addition to fatalities caused directly by Israeli airstrikes, drones, artillery, and gunfire, the deprivation of basic necessities has been utilized as a weapon of war. This includes a lack of shelter during severe weather and acute shortages of food and essential supplies due to ongoing aid restrictions. Simultaneously, the healthcare system has been a primary target of military operations. articles.title: Anti-austerity protests continue with force in France
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Half a million people took part in demonstrations across France on Tuesday, November 17, in response to a strike call by public sector workers. Tuesday’s strike and protests marked the continuation of a mobilization wave that has shaken the country for approximately two months. “Today was the eleventh round of demonstrations since September 29,” wrote the General Confederation of Labor (CGT). “All in all, in two months, over 5 million demonstrators joined the mobilization for our public services and against the cost of living crisis.” Watch: France’s protest movement is fighting more than Macron “Workers continue to demonstrate their rejection of austerity policies, the deterioration of public services and the erosion of purchasing power,” echoed the trade union organization Solidaires . “

articles.title: Why I joined Tempest
articles.author: Keegan O'Brien
articles.content_excerpt: I’ m writing this message from Belfast, Northern Ireland. I’m on a solo trip around the country, and it’s been absolutely stunning. If you haven’t been to Ireland, I highly recommend making the trip! Today, I visited the James Connolly Museum, and the experience moved me to share some photos and brief reflections about my political life. These past seven-plus years since the dissolution of the International Socialist Organization have been a politically challenging time for me as a revolutionary socialist, as I know they have been for many others. At times, I still feel like I’ve lost my political home and anchor, struggling to stay afloat, make sense of what’s happening in the world, and figure out what comes next. articles.title: “Little Hands, Big Change”: 8-Year-Old Kenyan Climate Champion Marren Akeyo Speaks Out at COP31
articles.content_excerpt: At the U.N. climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, Little Miss Environment Kenya 2026, Marren Akeyo, addressed world leaders on their responsibility to take real action to stop climate change. “Climate change does not ask for your birth certificate before affecting you. So, why should we wait until we’re adults to protect our planet?” said 8-year-old Akeyo. “We are ready to grow food. We are ready to take care of our planet. But we need you to give us opportunities. Don’t just tell us, ’You’re the leaders of tomorrow.’ Let us lead something today. Start with what you have.”
